paper_title: Towards Automatic Generation of Shareable Clinical Notes
core_problem: Patient privacy concerns hinder the open dissemination of invaluable large-scale clinical data, and existing de-identification methods are susceptible to adversarial attacks.
methodology_summary: Proposing to automatically generate synthetic clinical notes using generative models trained on real de-identified records, specifically focusing on unstructured natural language data from clinical notes.
empirical_results: Neural language models yield synthetic notes whose utility is close to that of real notes in some clinical NLP tasks, while also measuring privacy preservation properties.
explicit_limitations: The generated notes, while useful, still leave ample room for future improvements, and early naive models (e.g., unigram distribution) disregard word context.
